symbols.name: \(\mathcal Y\)
symbols.def: The state space of the observed and potential outcomes.

symbols.name: \(a\)
symbols.def: The treatment arm whose counterfactual law is studied.

symbols.name: \(Y(0),Y(1)\)
symbols.def: The two potential outcomes under the binary treatment interventions.

symbols.name: \(e\)
symbols.def: The scalar probability \(e=\Pr(A=a)\) in the fixed covariate stratum.

symbols.name: \(R\)
symbols.def: The residual law representing \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A\ne a)\).

symbols.name: \(f\)
symbols.space: finite continuous convex functions \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\)
symbols.def: The generator of the mutual-absolute-continuity version of the Jung--Kang divergence ambiguity class.

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\)
symbols.def: The one-sided likelihood-ratio class defined in \(\mathrm{def:mixture\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak H_c\)
symbols.space: class of finite continuous convex generators

symbols.name: \(p\)
symbols.def: The scalar \(p=P(B)\) for a measurable event \(B\subseteq\mathcal Y\).

symbols.name: \(q_0\)
symbols.def: The boundary coordinate \(q_0=ep\) for a full-support binary observational law.

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon\)
symbols.def: A positive perturbation for the binary candidate probability \(q=ep-\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: \(q\)
symbols.def: The success probability in the binary candidate law \(Q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\).

symbols.name: \(y\)
symbols.def: A generic threshold indexing the counterfactual CDF.

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: A measurable bounded function whose counterfactual expectation is bounded.

symbols.name: \(\underline\theta_h,\overline\theta_h\)
symbols.def: The infimum and supremum of \(E_Q[h]\) over \(Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal O_f\)
symbols.def: The stable ball-feasible but SCM-illegal region delivered by \(\mathrm{thm:open\text{-}illegal\text{-}dichotomy}\).

symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: The number of independent observational units.

assumptions.condition: The observed vertices \(A,Y\) have the bow ADMG \(A\to Y\) and \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), represented by a nonparametric latent-variable SCM.

standard.name: Nonparametric SCM Markov to a bow ADMG

assumptions.condition: The realized outcome satisfies \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely.
Every candidate bow SCM satisfies \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)\sim\mathcal L(Y(a))\).

standard.name: Mutual absolute continuity of observational and interventional arm laws

assumptions.condition: The observations \((A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed draws from the observed bow-SCM law.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y): Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))\text{ in a bow-ADMG SCM with }\Pr(A=a)=e,\ \mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P,\text{ and member properties }\mathrm{ass:bow\text{-}structure},\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:positivity},\mathrm{ass:mutual\text{-}ac}\}\). At the boundary, define \(\mathfrak M_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e\le1\), \(\mathfrak L_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y): Q=eP+(1-e)R\text{ for some }R\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\text{ with }R\ll P\}\); hence \(\mathfrak L_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_c\)
definitions.construction: \(\{f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R: f\text{ is finite, continuous, convex, }f(1)=0,\text{ and there exists }b\in\mathbb R\text{ such that }g_b(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\text{ obeys }g_b(t)=0\text{ for }0\le t\le c\text{ and }g_b(t)>0\text{ for }t>c\}\).

definitions.name: \(L_e,U_e\)
definitions.construction: For \(0\le e\le1\), \(L_e(p)=e p\) for \(0\le p<1\), \(L_e(1)=1\), \(U_e(0)=0\), and \(U_e(p)=e p+1-e\) for \(0<p\le1\). In particular, \(L_1(p)=U_1(p)=p\) for every \(p\in[0,1]\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: Let \(n_a=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\), \(\delta_e=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n)}\), and \(\delta_F=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n_a)}\) when \(n_a>0\). Form \(I_e=[\widehat e_n-\delta_e,\widehat e_n+\delta_e]\cap[0,1]\) and \(I_F(y)=[\widehat F_{P,n}(y)-\delta_F,\widehat F_{P,n}(y)+\delta_F]\cap[0,1]\). For every \(y\), \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\) is the coordinatewise rectangular hull of \(\{(L_\eta(p),U_\eta(p)):\eta\in I_e,\ p\in I_F(y)\}\); when \(n_a=0\), set it to \([0,1]^2\).

definitions.name: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\)
definitions.construction: Handle: linearize the joint pre-endpoint empirical process \((\widehat e_n,\widehat F_{P,n})\), derive the Hadamard directional derivative of the piecewise map \((e,F_P)\mapsto(L_e\circ F_P,U_e\circ F_P)\), and estimate that derivative inside a Fang--Santos multiplier or numerical-delta bootstrap before taking the supremum over thresholds and arms.

statements.statement: For every standard Borel \(\mathcal Y\), arm \(a\), probability law \(P\), and \(0<e<1\), the bow-ADMG compatible interventional laws are exactly the propensity mixtures: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\). Equivalently, \(Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\) if and only if \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for some \(R\ll P\), or if and only if \(Q\sim P\) and \(dP/dQ\le1/e\) \(Q\)-almost surely. Every admissible \(R\) is realized by a latent construction with \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\).
statements.justification: This structural input identifies the exact compatible-SCM law set needed by the flagship generator frontier.
statements.gap: Jung and Kang (2026, Assumption 4; Theorem 5, equations (3)--(4); proof in Appendix E) prove that compatible interventional laws lie in the calibrated ambiguity class, while Huber contamination results do not prove realization by the specified bow SCM.
statements.consumer: It supplies the legal feasible set for every downstream distributional or expectation bound in \(\texttt{itbound}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\), an arm \(a\), and a bow-SCM belonging to \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\).  By consistency,
\[
 \mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)=\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P.
\]
Put \(R=\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A\ne a)\).  The law of total probability, with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\), gives
\[
 Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))=eP+(1-e)R. \tag{1}
\]
The mutual-absolute-continuity assumption says \(P\sim Q\).  If \(N\) is measurable and \(P(N)=0\), then \(Q(N)=0\), and (1), nonnegativity, and \(1-e>0\) imply \(R(N)=0\).  Thus \(R\ll P\), proving \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak L_e(P)\).

Conversely, suppose that \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for a probability law \(R\ll P\).  On a standard Borel probability space construct \(A\) with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\).  Conditionally on \(A=a\), draw \(Y(a)\) with law \(P\); conditionally on \(A\ne a\), draw \(Y(a)\) with law \(R\).  Draw the other potential outcome \(Y(1-a)\) conditionally independently with any fixed law, for example \(P\).  Take the single latent variable
\[
 U=(A,Y(0),Y(1)),
\]
set the treatment structural equation to the first coordinate of \(U\), and set the outcome structural equation to \(Y=Y(A)\).  This is a latent-variable representation of the bow ADMG: the common latent parent \(U\) supplies \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), while the outcome equation has the direct input \(A\), supplying \(A\to Y\).  It obeys consistency by construction, has the specified propensity and observed arm law, and (1) gives \(\mathcal L(Y(a))=Q\).  Moreover, \(Q\ll P\) because \(R\ll P\), and \(P\ll Q\) because \(Q(B)\ge eP(B)\) for every measurable \(B\).  Hence \(P\sim Q\), so the constructed SCM belongs to \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\).  This proves the reverse inclusion and the asserted realization.

It remains to verify the likelihood-ratio formulation.  If \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with \(R\ll P\), then \(Q\sim P\), and \(Q\ge eP\) implies
\[
 \frac{dP}{dQ}\le \frac1e\qquad Q\text{-almost surely}. \tag{2}
\]
Conversely, if \(Q\sim P\) and (2) holds, define
\[
 R(B)=\frac{Q(B)-eP(B)}{1-e}.
\]
Writing \(r=dP/dQ\), the numerator has density \(1-er\ge0\) with respect to \(Q\); it therefore defines a nonnegative countably additive measure.  Its total mass is \((1-e)/(1-e)=1\), and \(R\ll P\) follows from \(Q\ll P\).  Thus \(R\) is an admissible residual law and \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\), completing all equivalences.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(c=1/e\). For every finite continuous convex \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) on every standard Borel space; this equality holds for every full-support binary \(P\); and \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\). Thus, modulo the divergence-invariant affine term \(b(t-1)\), exactness holds if and only if the generator vanishes on \([0,1/e]\) and is strictly positive on \((1/e,\infty)\).
statements.justification: This is the flagship result: the affine-invariant iff identifies precisely which divergence ambiguity classes are causally complete rather than merely valid outer sets.
statements.gap: Fauss, Zoubir, and Poor (2018) preserve least-favorable tests under a constructed density band and ask when uncertainty sets themselves coincide; Jung and Kang (2026) do not characterize the generators giving set equality.
statements.consumer: Divergence designers obtain a complete rule for selecting a propensity-calibrated generator whose feasible laws are exactly the bow-SCM laws.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(c=1/e\).  We first record directly from convexity that the likelihood-ratio class is always inside the divergence ball.  If \(Q\sim P\), \(r=dP/dQ\le c\), and \(E_Qr=1\), then the chord inequality on \([0,c]\) gives
\[
 f(r)\le \left(1-\frac r c\right)f(0)+\frac r c f(c).
\]
Integration yields
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)\le \left(1-\frac1c\right)f(0)+\frac1c f(c)
 =(1-e)f(0)+ef(1/e)=B_f(e). \tag{3}
\]
By the likelihood-ratio equivalence in \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\), (3) proves \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\).

Suppose first that \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\).  Choose \(b\) from the definition and put \(g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\).  Since \(E_Q[dP/dQ]=1\),
\[
 D_g(P\|Q)=D_f(P\|Q),
\]
and, because \(ec=1\),
\[
 B_g(e)=B_f(e)-b\{e(c-1)+(1-e)(0-1)\}=B_f(e). \tag{4}
\]
For this representative, \(B_g(e)=0\), \(g=0\) on \([0,c]\), and \(g>0\) on \((c,\infty)\).  Therefore
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)\le B_f(e)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \int g(dP/dQ)\,dQ=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{dP}{dQ}\le c\quad Q\text{-almost surely}. \tag{5}
\]
The last equivalence uses the pointwise nonnegativity of \(g\) and its strict positivity above \(c\).  Combining (5) with the likelihood-ratio characterization proves \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\) on every standard Borel space.

For necessity, assume equality of the two classes for every full-support binary \(P\).  Because \(f\) is finite and convex and \(1\) is an interior point of its domain, the left and right secant slopes at \(1\) bound a finite supporting slope \(b\): convexity gives a number \(b\) satisfying
\[
 f(t)\ge f(1)+b(t-1)=b(t-1),\qquad t\ge0.
\]
Set \(g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\).  Then \(g\ge0\), \(g(1)=0\), and (4) shows that both the divergence and radius are unchanged.

For each \(x\in(0,1)\), let
\[
 \lambda_x=\frac{1-x}{c-x},\qquad
 Q_x=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\lambda_x),\qquad
 P_x=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(c\lambda_x).
\]
Both binary laws have full support, and the two values of \(dP_x/dQ_x\) are \(c\) and \(x\).  Hence \(Q_x\in\mathfrak L_e(P_x)\).  We claim
\[
 D_g(P_x\|Q_x)=B_g(e). \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, (3) gives the weak inequality.  If it were strict, keep \(x\) fixed, replace \(c\) by \(t>c\), and set \(\lambda(t)=(1-x)/(t-x)\), \(Q_t=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\lambda(t))\), and \(P_t=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(t\lambda(t))\).  The divergence
\[
 \lambda(t)g(t)+(1-\lambda(t))g(x)
\]
is continuous at \(t=c\).  It would remain below \(B_g(e)\) for all sufficiently small \(t-c>0\), although \(dP_t/dQ_t=t>c\) on the success atom.  This would put \(Q_t\) in the ball but outside \(\mathfrak L_e(P_t)\), contradicting binary set equality.  Thus (6) holds.

Letting \(x\uparrow1\) in (6), continuity of \(g\), \(g(1)=0\), and \(\lambda_x\to0\) give \(B_g(e)=0\).  Since
\[
 B_g(e)=\frac1c g(c)+\left(1-\frac1c\right)g(0)
\]
and both summands are nonnegative with positive coefficients, \(g(0)=g(c)=0\).  Convexity gives \(g(t)\le0\) between these endpoints, while the supporting-line construction gives \(g(t)\ge0\); hence \(g=0\) on \([0,c]\).  Finally, if \(g(t_0)=0\) for some \(t_0>c\), choose any \(x\in(0,1)\) and form the preceding binary pair with likelihood ratios \(t_0,x\).  It is illegal, but its divergence is zero and its radius is zero, another contradiction.  Therefore \(g(t)>0\) for every \(t>c\), so \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\).

Universal equality plainly implies equality for every full-support binary law; the preceding paragraph proves that binary equality implies membership in \(\mathfrak H_c\), and (5) proves that membership implies universal equality.  This closes the three-way equivalence.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\), let \(c=1/e\), and suppose \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\). There is a nonempty Euclidean-open set \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) of binary pairs \((p,q)\), interpreted as \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) and \(Q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), such that \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L_e(P)\) throughout \(\mathcal O_f\). More precisely, either no affine representative of \(f\) is affine on \([0,c]\), in which case \(\mathcal O_f\) can be chosen with \(D_f(P\|Q)<B_f(e)\), or an affine representative vanishes on \([0,c]\) and on \([0,d]\) for some \(d>c\), in which case an open illegal set is contained in the zero-divergence face. This dichotomy includes nondifferentiable and piecewise-linear generators.
statements.justification: This stable converse certifies that every failure of the flagship frontier persists under perturbation and is not a hand-tuned counterexample.
statements.gap: Sason and Verdu (2016) analyze hinge divergences and bounded likelihood ratios, while Guntuboyina, Saha, and Schiebinger (2014) reduce divergence extrema to small alphabets; neither proves this fully quantified open-set dichotomy for every finite convex generator.
statements.consumer: The result gives a robust legality diagnostic for KL, Hellinger, chi-square, total-variation, Jensen--Shannon, and every other failing generator.
statements.proof_tex:
As in the preceding theorem, choose a supporting slope \(b\) at \(1\), put \(g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\), and note that \(g\ge0\), \(g(1)=0\), \(D_g=D_f\), and \(B_g(e)=B_f(e)\).  There are exactly two cases.

First suppose that \(f\), equivalently every affine representative of \(f\), is not affine on \([0,c]\).  Then \(g\) is not identically zero there.  If both \(g(0)\) and \(g(c)\) were zero, convexity and nonnegativity would force \(g=0\) on \([0,c]\), a contradiction.  Thus
\[
 B_g(e)=\frac1c g(c)+\left(1-\frac1c\right)g(0)>0. \tag{7}
\]
Fix any \(t>c\).  For \(x\in(0,1)\), define
\[
 \lambda(t,x)=\frac{1-x}{t-x},\quad
 q(t,x)=\lambda(t,x),\quad
 p(t,x)=t\lambda(t,x).
\]
These numbers lie in \((0,1)\), and the likelihood ratios of \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p(t,x))\) relative to \(Q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q(t,x))\) are \(t\) and \(x\).  Hence the pair is illegal because \(t>c\).  Moreover,
\[
 D_g(P\|Q)=\lambda(t,x)g(t)+(1-\lambda(t,x))g(x)\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{as }x\uparrow1. \tag{8}
\]
By (7)--(8), some \(x\) gives strict ball feasibility.  On \((0,1)^2\), the binary divergence
\[
 (p,q)\longmapsto qf(p/q)+(1-q)f((1-p)/(1-q))
\]
is continuous.  The conditions that this expression be strictly below \(B_f(e)\) and that one likelihood ratio exceed \(c\) are open.  A sufficiently small Euclidean neighborhood of the constructed pair is therefore a nonempty open set \(\mathcal O_f\) contained in \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L_e(P)\), with strict divergence inequality.

Second suppose that \(f\) is affine on \([0,c]\).  Taking \(b\) to be that affine slope makes \(g=0\) on \([0,c]\); convexity makes this line supporting, so \(g\ge0\) everywhere.  Since \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), there exists \(d>c\) with \(g(d)=0\).  Convexity and nonnegativity then force \(g=0\) on all of \([0,d]\), and consequently \(B_g(e)=0\).  Choose \(t\in(c,d)\) and \(x\in(0,1)\), and use the same \((p(t,x),q(t,x))\).  In a sufficiently small open neighborhood, the two likelihood ratios remain in \((0,d)\), while the first remains above \(c\).  Throughout that neighborhood,
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)=D_g(P\|Q)=0=B_g(e)=B_f(e),
\]
so the neighborhood is an open illegal subset of the zero-divergence face.  The argument uses only finiteness, continuity, and convexity; no differentiability is invoked, and it applies unchanged to piecewise-linear generators.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(p\in(0,1)\), let \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), and set \(q_0=ep\). For \(f_{\mathrm{KL}}(t)=t\log t\), \(B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e)=-\log e\) and \[D_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(P\|\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_0))=p\log(1/e)+(1-p)\log\!\left(\frac{1-p}{1-ep}\right)<-\log e=B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e).\] Hence continuity implies that every sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\) obeys \(D_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(P\|\operatorname{Bernoulli}(ep-\varepsilon))<B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e)\), while \(p/(ep-\varepsilon)>1/e\). Thus \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(ep-\varepsilon)\in\mathfrak B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}},e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L_e(P)\), and the strict inequalities persist on a binary open neighborhood.
statements.justification: The KL calculation is a transparent interior witness that the ambiguity class can contain laws violating the causal likelihood-ratio cap.
statements.gap: Jung and Kang (2026) establish validity of the KL ambiguity class as an outer causal bound but do not test realizability of its interior binary members by the bow SCM.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{itbound}\) IHDP audit obtains a closed-form unit test for detecting an omitted cap constraint in its KL program.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}positivity}\), \(0<e<1\).  Since \(p\in(0,1)\), the Bernoulli law \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) has full support on \(\{0,1\}\), and \(q_0=ep\) belongs to \((0,1)\).  The convention \(0\log 0=0\) gives \(f_{\mathrm{KL}}(0)=0\), whereas
\[
 f_{\mathrm{KL}}(1/e)=\frac1e\log(1/e).
\]
Consequently, by the definition of \(B_f(e)\),
\[
 B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e)
 =e f_{\mathrm{KL}}(1/e)+(1-e)f_{\mathrm{KL}}(0)
 =\log(1/e)=-\log e.
\]

Let \(Q_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_0)\).  Both \(P\) and \(Q_0\) have full support, so \(P\sim Q_0\), in particular \(P\ll Q_0\), as required in the definition of \(D_f(P\|Q)\).  On the atoms \(1\) and \(0\), respectively, the likelihood ratio \(dP/dQ_0\) is \(p/q_0\) and \((1-p)/(1-q_0)\).  Therefore that definition and \(q_0=ep\) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(P\|Q_0)
 &=q_0\frac{p}{q_0}\log\!\left(\frac{p}{q_0}\right)
   +(1-q_0)\frac{1-p}{1-q_0}
       \log\!\left(\frac{1-p}{1-q_0}\right)\\
 &=p\log(1/e)+(1-p)\log\!\left(\frac{1-p}{1-ep}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The gap from the radius can be computed without an inequality relaxation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e)-D_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(P\|Q_0)
 &=(1-p)\left\{\log(1/e)-
       \log\!\left(\frac{1-p}{1-ep}\right)\right\}\\
 &=(1-p)\log\!\left(\frac{1-ep}{e(1-p)}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(e(1-p)>0\), and
\[
 (1-ep)-e(1-p)=1-e>0.
\]
Thus \((1-ep)/(e(1-p))>1\); strict monotonicity of the logarithm and \(1-p>0\) show that the displayed gap is strictly positive.  This proves the asserted strict inequality at \(q_0\).

For \(q\in(0,1)\), put
\[
 K_p(q)=p\log\!\left(\frac p q\right)
       +(1-p)\log\!\left(\frac{1-p}{1-q}\right).
\]
The logarithm is continuous on \((0,\infty)\), so \(K_p\) is continuous on \((0,1)\).  If
\[
 s=B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e)-K_p(q_0)>0,
\]
continuity at \(q_0\) supplies \(\delta>0\) such that \(|q-q_0|<\delta\) and \(q\in(0,1)\) imply \(|K_p(q)-K_p(q_0)|<s/2\).  Hence, for every
\[
 0<\varepsilon<\min\{\delta,ep\},
 \qquad q=ep-\varepsilon,
\]
one has \(q\in(0,1)\) and
\[
 D_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}\!\left(P\middle\|\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\right)
 =K_p(q)<K_p(q_0)+\frac{s}{2}<B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e).
\]
The two Bernoulli laws again have full support and hence are mutually absolutely continuous.  The definition \(\mathrm{def{:}jk\text{-}ball}\) now gives
\[
 \operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\in\mathfrak B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}},e}(P).
\]

It remains to prove incompatibility with the mixture class rather than merely assert it.  If \(Q\in\mathfrak L_e(P)\), then by \(\mathrm{def{:}mixture\text{-}class}\) there is a probability law \(R\ll P\) such that \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\).  Evaluating this equality on the success atom \(\{1\}\) gives
\[
 Q(\{1\})=ep+(1-e)R(\{1\})\ge ep,
\]
where \(1-e>0\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass{:}positivity}\) and \(R(\{1\})\ge0\) because \(R\) is a probability law.  Our candidate instead has \(Q(\{1\})=q=ep-\varepsilon<ep\), equivalently
\[
 \frac{p}{q}>\frac1e,
\]
where division is legitimate because \(e,p,q>0\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Bernoulli}(ep-\varepsilon)
 \in\mathfrak B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}},e}(P)
 \setminus\mathfrak L_e(P).
\]

Finally, the claimed neighborhood statement is also strict.  Fix any \(\varepsilon\) in the preceding range and write \(q=ep-\varepsilon\).  On the open square \(\Omega=(0,1)^2\), define
\[
 \Phi(p',q')=p'\log\!\left(\frac{p'}{q'}\right)
 +(1-p')\log\!\left(\frac{1-p'}{1-q'}\right).
\]
Both maps
\[
 (p',q')\longmapsto B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e)-\Phi(p',q')
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (p',q')\longmapsto ep'-q'
\]
are continuous on \(\Omega\), and both are strictly positive at \((p,q)\).  Their positive inverse images have an open intersection \(\mathcal U\subseteq\Omega\) containing \((p,q)\).  For every \((p',q')\in\mathcal U\), the full-support laws \(P'=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p')\) and \(Q'=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q')\) satisfy \(D_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(P'\|Q')<B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}}}(e)\) and \(q'<ep'\).  The first strict inequality and \(P'\sim Q'\) put \(Q'\) in \(\mathfrak B_{f_{\mathrm{KL}},e}(P')\); the event calculation above excludes it from \(\mathfrak L_e(P')\).  Thus the illegal certificate persists throughout a binary open neighborhood, as required.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\), set \(c=1/e\), and let \(f_c(t)=(t-c)_+\). Then \(B_{f_c}(e)=0\). For \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) and \(Q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\) with \(p,q\in(0,1)\), \[D_{f_c}(P\|Q)=(p-cq)_+ + ((1-p)-c(1-q))_+.\] Consequently, \(D_{f_c}(P\|Q)=0\) if and only if \(ep\le q\le1-e+ep\), exactly the binary propensity-mixture fiber. Positive scaling of \(f_c\) and addition of any affine term \(b(t-1)\) leave this zero-radius exactness certificate unchanged.
statements.justification: The hinge calculation displays the cap-detecting mechanism underlying the flagship iff on the minimal alphabet.
statements.gap: Sason and Verdu (2016) develop \(E_\gamma\)-hinge divergences, but the binary equality with the propensity-mixture fiber and its affine invariance are not stated as a bow-SCM legality certificate.
statements.consumer: Divergence designers obtain a two-cell regression test showing that a proposed implementation recovers the exact lawful interval.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{ass:positivity}\), \(0<e<1\), and hence \(c=1/e>1\).  Therefore
\[
f_c(c)=(c-c)_+=0,
\qquad
f_c(0)=(0-c)_+=0.
\]
Using the definition of \(B_f(e)\), it follows that
\[
B_{f_c}(e)=e f_c(1/e)+(1-e)f_c(0)
=e f_c(c)+(1-e)f_c(0)=0.
\]

Put the two points of the Bernoulli outcome space in the order \(1,0\).  Since
\(p,q\in(0,1)\), both \(P\) and \(Q\) assign strictly positive mass to both
points.  Thus \(P\sim Q\), as required by \(\mathrm{def:jk\text{-}ball}\), and
the two Radon--Nikodym ratios are
\[
\frac{dP}{dQ}(1)=\frac pq,
\qquad
\frac{dP}{dQ}(0)=\frac{1-p}{1-q}.
\]
The definition of \(D_f(P\|Q)\) consequently gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_{f_c}(P\|Q)
&=q\left(\frac pq-c\right)_+
 +(1-q)\left(\frac{1-p}{1-q}-c\right)_+\\
&=(p-cq)_+ + ((1-p)-c(1-q))_+.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the second equality uses \(s(x/s-c)_+=(x-cs)_+\), first with
\(s=q>0\) and then with \(s=1-q>0\).

Both summands in the last display are nonnegative, so their sum is zero if and
only if each is zero.  Since \(x_+=0\) if and only if \(x\le 0\), and since
\(1/c=e\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_{f_c}(P\|Q)=0
&\Longleftrightarrow p-cq\le0
 \ \text{and}\ (1-p)-c(1-q)\le0\\
&\Longleftrightarrow q\ge \frac pc=ep
 \ \text{and}\ q\le 1-\frac{1-p}{c}=1-e+ep.
\end{aligned}
\]
It remains to verify that this interval is exactly the fiber specified by
\(\mathrm{def:mixture\text{-}class}\).  If
\(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) and \(R=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(r)\), then evaluation at
the point \(1\) yields
\[
q=ep+(1-e)r.
\]
Because \(r\in[0,1]\), this implies \(ep\le q\le ep+1-e\).  Conversely, if
\(ep\le q\le1-e+ep\), define
\[
r=\frac{q-ep}{1-e}.
\]
The denominator is strictly positive by \(\mathrm{ass:positivity}\), and the
two interval inequalities give \(0\le r\le1\).  Hence
\(R=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(r)\) is a probability law and
\(Q=eP+(1-e)R\).  Moreover, because \(p\in(0,1)\), \(P\) has full support on
the binary space, so every such \(R\) satisfies \(R\ll P\).  This proves the
claimed equality with the binary fiber of \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\).

Finally, let \(\lambda>0\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\), and define
\(\widetilde f(t)=\lambda f_c(t)+b(t-1)\).  Since \(c>1\), one has
\(f_c(1)=0\); positive scaling preserves convexity and addition of an affine
function preserves convexity, so \(\widetilde f\) is finite, continuous,
convex, and \(\widetilde f(1)=0\).  In the terminology of
\(\mathrm{def:hinge\text{-}class}\), subtracting \(b(t-1)\) leaves
\(\lambda f_c(t)\), which vanishes on \([0,c]\) and is strictly positive on
\((c,\infty)\).  Its radius is still zero because \(ec=1\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
B_{\widetilde f}(e)
&=e\{\lambda f_c(c)+b(c-1)\}
 +(1-e)\{\lambda f_c(0)-b\}\\
&=b\{e(c-1)-(1-e)\}=b(ec-1)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Also, since \(P\ll Q\) and both are probability laws,
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_{\widetilde f}(P\|Q)
&=\lambda D_{f_c}(P\|Q)
 +b\int_{\mathcal Y}\left(\frac{dP}{dQ}-1\right)dQ\\
&=\lambda D_{f_c}(P\|Q)+b\{P(\mathcal Y)-Q(\mathcal Y)\}
=\lambda D_{f_c}(P\|Q).
\end{aligned}
\]
As \(\lambda>0\), the last quantity vanishes exactly when
\(D_{f_c}(P\|Q)\) vanishes.  Thus positive scaling and addition of
\(b(t-1)\) leave both the zero radius and the exact binary legality fiber
unchanged.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal Y=\mathbb R\). For every threshold \(y\), write \(p=F_P(y)\). The exact bow-SCM identified interval is \(\{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]\). Each endpoint is attained by a bow-ADMG SCM satisfying all maintained support conditions, including when \(P\) has an atom at \(y\), \(p=0\), or \(p=1\). For \(0<p<1\), the witnesses choose residual laws supported on \(({-}\infty,y]\) or its complement; the boundary formulas force the unique value \(0\) or \(1\).
statements.justification: This consequence converts the structural mixture input into closed-form distributional endpoints and handles atoms correctly.
statements.gap: Huber contamination gives the scalar mixture geometry and Duarte et al. (2024) certify discrete SCM bounds computationally, but neither supplies these continuous-outcome bow-SCM endpoints with explicit attainment under mutual absolute continuity.
statements.consumer: Researchers reporting counterfactual CDFs or quantiles can replace relaxed divergence endpoints by exact, directly evaluable causal envelopes.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a threshold \(y\), put \(B=(-\infty,y]\), and write \(p=P(B)\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\), every compatible law and only such a law has the form \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with \(R\ll P\).  Therefore, with \(r_B=R(B)\),
\[
 F_Q(y)=Q(B)=ep+(1-e)r_B. \tag{9}
\]
If \(0<p<1\), absolute continuity permits every \(r_B\in[0,1]\): the two endpoint residual laws are
\[
 R_1(C)=\frac{P(C\cap B)}{p},\qquad
 R_0(C)=\frac{P(C\cap B^c)}{1-p},
\]
and their convex mixtures attain every intermediate value.  Equation (9) therefore ranges over \([ep,ep+1-e]=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]\).  The completeness theorem turns each such residual law into an attaining bow-ADMG SCM satisfying consistency, positivity, and mutual absolute continuity.

If \(p=0\), then \(R\ll P\) forces \(R(B)=0\), so (9) is uniquely zero, equal to \(L_e(0)=U_e(0)\).  If \(p=1\), then \(P(B^c)=0\) forces \(R(B^c)=0\), so (9) is uniquely one, equal to \(L_e(1)=U_e(1)\).  These arguments depend only on the event and its complement and hence remain valid when \(P\) has an atom at \(y\).  They also provide the claimed attaining SCMs in every case.

statements.statement: For every admissible generator \(f\), \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak M_e(P)\). For each \(h\in L^\infty(P)\), the exact support-function endpoints are \(\underline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_P h\) and \(\overline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_P h\). Consequently, adding \(dP/dQ\le1/e\) to every \(\texttt{itbound}\) divergence program is weakly tighter for every query and every dataset; it is strictly tighter whenever a unique relaxed optimizer violates the cap. For every \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), some bounded binary query has a strict legality gap on a nonempty open region of observational laws.
statements.justification: This implementation layer turns the flagship legality frontier into an exact query-level correction and a checkable strictness condition.
statements.gap: Jung and Kang (2026) optimize exactly relative to their ambiguity classes and aggregate the resulting valid outer causal bounds, whereas Dorn and Guo (2023) show in another sensitivity model that enforcing the exact compatible class can strictly repair over-wide bounds.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{itbound}\) maintainers can implement one cap constraint across all supported divergences and re-audit the reported IHDP endpoints.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(Q\in\mathfrak L_e(P)\).  The likelihood-ratio characterization gives \(Q\sim P\) and \(r=dP/dQ\le c=1/e\).  Convexity of \(f\) on \([0,c]\) and \(E_Qr=1\) give the chord bound
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)
 \le \left(1-\frac1c\right)f(0)+\frac1c f(c)
 =(1-e)f(0)+ef(1/e)=B_f(e). \tag{10}
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\) for every finite continuous convex admissible generator.  By the definition of the lawful correction and \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\),
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)
 =\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\cap\mathfrak L_e(P)
 =\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak M_e(P). \tag{11}
\]

For \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\), linearity gives
\[
 E_Q[h]=eE_P[h]+(1-e)E_R[h]. \tag{12}
\]
Let \(m=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_P h\) and \(M=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_P h\), which are finite because \(h\in L^\infty(P)\).  Every \(R\ll P\) satisfies \(m\le E_Rh\le M\).  Conversely, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the sets \(\{h<m+\varepsilon\}\) and \(\{h>M-\varepsilon\}\) have positive \(P\)-probability by the definitions of essential infimum and supremum.  Normalizing \(P\) on these sets produces admissible residual laws whose expectations are at most \(m+\varepsilon\) and at least \(M-\varepsilon\), respectively.  Taking \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) in (12) proves
\[
 \underline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)m,\qquad
 \overline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)M. \tag{13}
\]

For the software claim, an empirical \(\texttt{itbound}\) program has finitely many probability-weight variables \((q_j)_j\).  Adding \(dP/dQ\le1/e\) is exactly the collection of closed linear inequalities \(q_j\ge ep_j\); by (11) it replaces the relaxed feasible set by the lawful one.  Set inclusion makes every lower-bound minimization weakly increase and every upper-bound maximization weakly decrease.  The lawful polytope is nonempty and compact, so a linear bounded-query objective attains its lawful optimum.  If the relaxed optimum is attained uniquely at a point violating the cap and the corrected optimum had the same value, the lawful attaining point would be a second relaxed optimizer, contradicting uniqueness.  Hence the correction is strict under the stated uniqueness condition.

Finally take the nonempty open binary illegal set from \(\mathrm{thm:open\text{-}illegal\text{-}dichotomy}\).  Illegality of a binary pair is exactly
\[
 q<ep\quad\text{or}\quad q>ep+1-e.
\]
At least one of these two open alternatives contains a nonempty open subset of \(\mathcal O_f\).  On that subset, for the bounded query equal to the success indicator, the relaxed ball contains the displayed \(q\), whereas (13) gives the lawful endpoint \(ep\) or \(ep+1-e\).  The corresponding relaxed lower or upper endpoint is therefore strictly outside the lawful endpoint.  Projection of this open subset onto the \(p\)-coordinate is nonempty and open, proving the asserted open region of observational laws.

statements.statement: Under independent observational sampling, the band \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) satisfies \(\Pr\{(L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y)))\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\text{ for every }y\in\mathbb R\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\), including \(n_a=0\), arbitrary atoms, and contact with \(F_P(y)\in\{0,1\}\). The guarantee follows by combining a propensity Hoeffding interval with a conditional Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz band and propagating their joint rectangle through the full piecewise endpoint map.
statements.justification: This inference layer propagates the lawful endpoint consequence with an honest finite-sample simultaneous guarantee at nonsmooth boundary cases.
statements.gap: Masten, Poirier, and Zhang (2024) develop uniform bands over a sensitivity index, and Jung and Kang (2026) give scalar orthogonal inference; neither covers the threshold-indexed lawful endpoint pair with boundary contacts.
statements.consumer: The IHDP audit can report simultaneous uncertainty for the complete corrected CDF envelope rather than pointwise error bars.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(E_e=\{e\in I_e\}\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:hoeffding\text{-}bounded\text{-}mean}\) to \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\).  With \(\delta_e=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n)}\),
\[
 \Pr(E_e^c)\le2e^{-2n\delta_e^2}=\alpha/2. \tag{14}
\]
Conditional on the complete treatment vector and on \(n_a>0\), independence of the sampled pairs implies that the \(n_a\) selected outcomes are independent with common conditional distribution \(P=\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)\).  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:dkw\text{-}massart\text{-}cdf\text{-}band}\), applied conditionally with sample size \(n_a\), gives
\[
 \Pr\left\{\left.\sup_y|\widehat F_{P,n}(y)-F_P(y)|>\delta_F\ \right|\ (A_i)_{i=1}^n\right\}
 \le2e^{-2n_a\delta_F^2}=\alpha/2. \tag{15}
\]
Let \(E_F\) denote the complementary simultaneous-CDF event when \(n_a>0\), and take \(E_F\) to hold automatically when \(n_a=0\).  Averaging (15) over the treatment vector yields \(\Pr(E_F^c)\le\alpha/2\).  The union bound with (14) gives
\[
 \Pr(E_e\cap E_F)\ge1-\alpha. \tag{16}
\]

On \(E_e\cap E_F\) and \(n_a>0\), the actual pair \((e,F_P(y))\) belongs to \(I_e\times I_F(y)\) simultaneously for every \(y\).  Hence the image point
\[
 (L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y)))
\]
belongs to the set whose coordinatewise rectangular hull defines \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\).  This argument requires neither continuity nor differentiability of the piecewise endpoint map, so atoms and the values zero and one cause no exception.  If \(n_a=0\), the band is \([0,1]^2\) by definition and contains the endpoint pair automatically.  The corrected endpoint definition at \(e=0\) also makes the image set in the construction well typed whenever the clipped interval \(I_e\) contains zero.  Combining these observations with (16) proves the simultaneous finite-sample guarantee.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(m\ge1\), if \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) are independent random variables satisfying \(0\le Z_i\le1\) almost surely and \(\mu=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m E[Z_i]\), then for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr\left(\left|m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m Z_i-\mu\right|>t\right)\le2\exp(-2mt^2).
\]

For every integer \(m\ge1\), if \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are independent real random variables with common distribution function \(F\), and \(\widehat F_m\) is their empirical distribution function, then for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr\left(\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}|\widehat F_m(y)-F(y)|>t\right)\le2\exp(-2mt^2).
\]

source.locator: Section 2.14, Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz inequality with Massart's sharp constant

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).  Consider any sequence of rectangular simultaneous bands that has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over a local class containing a law with \(F_P(y_0)=1\) and alternatives with \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=1-\delta_n\), where \(\delta_n>0\) and \(n\delta_n\to0\).  Under the boundary law, with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\), the lower-endpoint projection of the band at \(y_0\) has diameter at least \(1-e-o(1)\).  The analogous assertion holds for the upper-endpoint projection when the class contains a law with \(F_P(y_0)=0\) and alternatives with \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=\delta_n\).  Consequently, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\) cannot yield a nonconservative shrinking band uniformly over such a tie-inclusive local class; derivative-aware inference is restricted to strata separated from these contacts, with \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) retained as the honest fallback.
statements.justification: This negative resolution isolates the discontinuity that prevents uniformly shrinking endpoint bands at drifting support contacts.
statements.gap: Fang and Santos (2019) provide derivative-aware bootstrap validity, but that device cannot overcome statistical indistinguishability across the discontinuous lawful endpoint faces proved here.
statements.consumer: The result delineates the separated regular strata where shorter directional bands may be used and retains the honest finite-sample band elsewhere.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a nonparametric bow-ADMG SCM in a fixed covariate stratum.
sampling_model.units: \((A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed; potential outcomes and the latent confounder are unobserved.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity \(0<e<1\) and mutual absolute continuity \(P\sim Q\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(e\) by the arm fraction and \(F_P\) by the empirical CDF within arm \(a\); the finite-sample band uses Hoeffding and conditional Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz radii.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumption 4, Theorem 5, equations (3)--(4), proves that every compatible interventional law lies in the propensity-calibrated \(f\)-divergence ambiguity class; the later optimization is exact relative to that ambiguity class, not a realizability theorem for every class member.
Its main theorem constructs density bands sharing the least-favorable pair of two divergence balls and its Discussion asks when the uncertainty sets themselves coincide.
Proposition 2.3 identifies Huber contamination with the forward linear-vacuous credal ball.
The paper develops functional domination and \(E_\gamma\) hinge tools for \(f\)-divergences under bounded relative information.
Theorem 2.1 reduces optimization under \(m\) divergence constraints to distributions on at most \(m+2\) points.
The paper reduces discrete causal bounding problems to polynomial programs and certifies sharpness by canonical response-function SCMs.
The paper constructs nonstandard-bootstrap confidence bands uniform over a scalar sensitivity index.

tldr: The flagship result classifies exactly when the mutual-absolute-continuity version of the Jung--Kang \(f\)-divergence ambiguity class equals the compatible binary-treatment bow-SCM fiber for every law: modulo affine generator terms, \(f\) must vanish through the propensity cap and be strictly positive above it. Bow-mixture completeness, \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with \(R\ll P\), supplies the structural input, and a universal open illegal binary region supplies the stable converse, with explicit KL and hinge certificates. Exact atom-aware CDF endpoints, bounded-query support functions, simultaneous bands, and the \(\texttt{itbound}\) and IHDP legality correction are consequences and implementation layers.

project_justification.gap: Jung and Kang prove that every compatible interventional law belongs to a propensity-calibrated ambiguity class and optimize exactly over that class, yielding valid outer causal bounds; they do not establish that every ambiguity-class member is realizable by a bow SCM. Robust-statistics and information-theory papers separately provide contamination neighborhoods, hinge divergences, density bands, and finite-alphabet reductions, but none identifies all ordinary convex generators whose calibrated class exactly equals the bow-SCM law class or proves an open illegal region for every failure.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a generator-level causal legality frontier: a necessary-and-sufficient affine-invariant condition, with stable counterexamples when it fails and explicit causal endpoints when the exact cap is imposed.
project_justification.fill: The propensity-hinge iff is the sole flagship. Bow-SCM mixture completeness supplies its structural input, and the nondifferentiability-robust binary open-gap theorem supplies its stable converse, including explicit KL and hinge certificates. Sharp CDF and bounded-query formulas, distribution-free confidence bands, and the shared software cap are consequences and implementation layers.

related_work: Jung and Kang (2026, Assumption 4; Theorem 5, equations (3)--(4); proof in Appendix E) prove that every compatible interventional law lies in the propensity-calibrated \(f\)-divergence ambiguity class, and their later optimization is exact relative to that class. Those ambiguity-class extrema are valid outer causal bounds; the paper does not establish that every member is realizable by a bow SCM, whereas the flagship target characterizes exactly when the ambiguity class equals the compatible bow-SCM fiber. This proposal uses the mutual-absolute-continuity version under their Assumption 4: their equation (10) visibly states only \(P\ll Q\), while the maintained model and density parametrization supply \(Q\ll P\). Sason and Verdu (2016) supply affine normalization, bounded-relative-information, and \(E_\gamma\)-hinge machinery that motivates the cap-detecting direction. Guntuboyina, Saha, and Schiebinger (2014, Theorem 2.1 and Section 3) show why divergence geometry can be exposed on small alphabets, while the proposed necessity proof specializes the boundary analysis to a binary propensity cap. Fauss, Zoubir, and Poor (2018, main theorem and Discussion) equate least-favorable robust tests under divergence balls and constructed density bands and explicitly leave set equality and generator recovery open; the proposed iff resolves that question for the one-sided propensity band. Chen, Berrett, Damoulas, and Caprio (2026, Proposition 2.3) identify Huber contamination with a linear-vacuous credal ball, which establishes the noncausal mixture geometry but not the ordinary \(f\)-generator frontier or bow-SCM realization. Duarte et al. (2024) certify sharp causal bounds by response-function polynomial programs for discrete variables; the proposed latent construction is analytic and covers general standard Borel outcomes. Dorn and Guo (2023) provide the closest econometric precedent for repairing an over-wide sensitivity optimization by imposing the exact compatible weighting class. Masten, Poirier, and Zhang (2024) and Fang and Santos (2019) motivate the uniform and derivative-aware inference layer, respectively.
technical_internal_limitation: Pointwise attainment of \(L_e(F_P(y))\) and \(U_e(F_P(y))\) permits the attaining residual law to depend on \(y\). It does not imply that the entire lower or upper envelope is itself one counterfactual CDF. The complete process identified set remains \(\{eF_P+(1-e)F_R:R\ll P\}\), so any reported whole curve must retain a common residual CDF.
honest_scope: The mixture characterization and endpoint algebra have short candidate arguments, but every result remains \(\mathrm{to\text{-}prove}\) at this stage. The load-bearing open content is the fully quantified necessity and open-illegal-region dichotomy for finite continuous convex generators with kinks or extended zero faces. The finite-sample band is deliberately conservative at support contacts; asymptotically exact tie-adaptive inference is isolated as \(\mathrm{oeq:tie\text{-}adaptive\text{-}exact\text{-}band}\). The mixture and SCM classes and the endpoint maps alone extend to the boundary \(e=1\), where \(\mathfrak M_1(P)=\mathfrak L_1(P)=\{P\}\) and \(L_1(p)=U_1(p)=p\). No all-generator singleton claim is made for calibrated divergence classes at \(e=1\): a zero-radius \(f\)-class is a singleton only under an additional strict Jensen-equality or cap-detecting condition, and affine or identically zero generators are counterexamples. The flagship iff remains explicitly fixed at \(0<e<1\). The empirical IHDP deliverable is a reproducible before-and-after audit, not a theorem about the benchmark.
